simple.meaning: הָבַל (hâbal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be vain in act, word, or expectation; specifically to lead astray.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in 2 Kings, Job, Psalms, Jeremiah, beginning at 2 Kings 17:15. The surrounding contexts include family, covenant.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָבַל (H1891) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: הָבַל (hâbal) / H1891 is traced through 2 Kings 17:15, Job 27:12, Psalms 62:11, Jeremiah 2:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to be vain in act, word, or expectation; specifically to lead astray
definitions.full: H1891. habal הָבַל verb denominative act emptily, become vain — Qal Jer 2:5 = 2Kin 17:15 they went after vanity וַיֶּהְבָּ֑לוּ and became vain , Psa 62:11 אַלתֶּֿהְבָּ֑לוּ וּבְגָזֵל do not become vain (i.e. be demoralized) by robbery; with cognate accusative Job 27:12 תֶּהְבָּ֑לוּ הֶבֶל זֶה לָמָּה why do ye become vain with vanity (i.e. shew yourselves utterly vain) ? Hiph`il cause to become vain Jer 23:16 (of false prophets) אֶתְכֶם הֵמָּה מַהְבִּלִים i.e. fill you with vain hopes.
